destinations.name: Marrakech
destinations.tagline: Souks, riads and the gateway to the Sahara
destinations.description: Lose yourself in the medina, sip mint tea on a rooftop and head out to the Atlas Mountains and the Agafay desert.

destinations.name: Fes
destinations.tagline: The medieval medina and the road to Merzouga
destinations.description: Fes el-Bali is the largest car-free medina in the world: 9,000 lanes of tanneries, madrasas and craft workshops. It is also the closest imperial city to the Erg Chebbi dunes, making it the classic starting point for Sahara tours that end in Marrakech.

destinations.name: Tangier
destinations.description: A ferry ride from Spain, Tangier is the natural start of a north-to-south journey: Chefchaouen's blue streets, the imperial cities, the Sahara and finally Marrakech.

destinations.name: Casablanca
destinations.description: Most international flights land in Casablanca. Start here with the Hassan II Mosque, then head inland to Rabat, the imperial cities, the desert and the mountains.

destinations.name: Chefchaouen
destinations.tagline: The Blue Pearl of the Rif mountains
destinations.description: Every wall, step and doorway in Chefchaouen's medina is washed in shades of blue. Wander quiet alleys, browse leather and weaving workshops, drink fresh orange juice in the squares and hike up to the Spanish Mosque for sunset.

destinations.name: Ouarzazate
destinations.description: Ouarzazate sits between the High Atlas and the Sahara, surrounded by kasbahs and film studios. It is the natural base for trips to Aït Benhaddou, the Draa Valley and the dunes.

destinations.name: Errachidia
destinations.tagline: The closest airport to the Merzouga dunes
destinations.description: Errachidia's Moulay Ali Cherif airport is about two hours from Erg Chebbi, making it the fastest way into the Sahara. Tours start at the airport or your hotel and head straight for the dunes.

destinations.name: Merzouga
destinations.description: The village at the foot of Erg Chebbi, Morocco's highest dunes. Base for camel treks, quad biking, sandboarding and nights in desert camps.

tours.title: Marrakech to Fes Luxury Desert Tour, 4 Days
tours.meetingPoint: Pickup from your hotel or riad in Marrakech
tours.excerpt: One way from Marrakech to Fes with a whole free day in the Sahara: nomad family visit, luxury camp and sunrise over Erg Chebbi.
tours.description:
This four-day private tour takes you one way from Marrakech to Fes and keeps a full day in the middle for the Sahara. Instead of just passing through Merzouga, you have a whole day around the Erg Chebbi dunes, including a visit to a Berber nomad family who live out beyond the sand.

On the way you cross the High Atlas to the kasbah of Aït Benhaddou, pass Ouarzazate, walk into the Todra Gorge and ride a camel into the dunes for a night in a luxury camp. The last day heads north to Fes through the palm groves and villages of the Ziz Valley.

Every part of the itinerary can be changed to suit your pace and interests.
highlights: Wide views over the High Atlas
Aït Benhaddou, a UNESCO World Heritage ksar
A walk into the Todra Gorge
Camel trek across the Erg Chebbi dunes
Sunset and sunrise over the dunes
Visit to a nomad family in the Sahara
Barbary macaques in the Middle Atlas cedar forest

itinerary.title: Day 1: Marrakech → High Atlas → Aït Benhaddou → Dadès Gorge
itinerary.details: Morning pickup from your accommodation in Marrakech. The road climbs over the High Atlas past Berber villages, with stops for photos along the way. In Aït Benhaddou you visit the kasbah, on the UNESCO list since 1987 and the backdrop for films and series such as Gladiator and Game of Thrones. After lunch, continue through Ouarzazate and the Valley of Roses to the Dadès Gorge, where you can see the rounded "monkey fingers" rocks before checking in for the night.

itinerary.title: Day 2: Dadès Gorge → Todra Gorge → Merzouga
itinerary.details: After breakfast, follow the Todra river through palm groves and villages to Tinghir and walk into the Todra Gorge, one of the most impressive canyons in the country. Then drive on to Merzouga. Your driver can stop at a Berber shop where you can try on traditional clothes for photos; buying anything (a scarf is handy in the desert) is entirely optional, and the stop can be skipped. In Merzouga you ride a camel into the dunes for sunset, try sandboarding, and spend the night in a luxury camp with dinner under the stars.

itinerary.title: Day 3: A full day in the Sahara
itinerary.details: Climb the nearest dune early for sunrise, then have breakfast at camp. A 4×4 takes you out to a nomad family living beyond the dunes, who show you how they live and explain their traditions. You also see the abandoned village of M’Fis, listen to Gnawa music in Khamlia and, when there is water, visit the seasonal Lake of Birds. After lunch, check in to a riad by the dunes with time to swim or walk on the sand. Dinner and the night are at the riad, or at the desert camp again if you prefer.

itinerary.title: Day 4: Merzouga → Ziz Valley → Ifrane → Fes
itinerary.details: After breakfast, set off for Fes with a stop at a viewpoint over the Ziz Valley. Lunch is in Midelt or along the way. Crossing the Middle Atlas cedar forest you may spot Barbary macaques, then stop in Ifrane for a break before arriving in Fes, where we drop you at your riad.

included: Pickup from your accommodation in Marrakech and drop-off in Fes
Private air-conditioned 4×4, van or minibus (depending on group size)
English-speaking private driver (or driver and guide); other languages on request
3 nights’ accommodation (hotel, luxury desert camp and riad)
notes: Driving times do not include stops for lunch and sightseeing.
Vegetarian, vegan and allergy needs can be catered for: tell us when you book.
The standard plan is a luxury camp on night two and a riad in Merzouga on night three. Ask if you would rather spend both nights at the camp.
You can also end back in Marrakech, or run this route in reverse from Fes to Marrakech.
Quad biking or buggy driving in the Erg Chebbi dunes can be added: just tell your driver.
Short on time? Ask about the 3-day version of this route.
Desert nights are in a luxury camp with private tents and en-suite bathrooms; we do not use basic or shared-bathroom camps.
From €239 per person; the final price depends on group size, accommodation and season.

Extras before, during or after the tour: airport transfers, a guided tour of Marrakech or Fes, a hot air balloon flight, day trips to Essaouira, Ouzoud, the Ourika Valley, Chefchaouen or Volubilis and Meknes, a desert photographer, a romantic dinner or proposal setup in the dunes.

pages.title: About Us
pages.content:
We are a small Moroccan travel agency specialising in desert tours, day trips and activities across Morocco. Our drivers and guides were born in the regions we travel through, from the Atlas mountains to the dunes of Erg Chebbi.

What we do

We run private and small-group tours that start from Marrakech, Fes, Casablanca, Tangier, Errachidia and Ouarzazate, as well as day trips, desert camping and activities such as camel rides, quad biking and hot air balloon flights.

How we work

  • Private by default: your own vehicle and driver, at your pace.
  • Flexible itineraries: every tour can be adjusted to your dates and interests.
  • Local team: we work with our own camps and trusted local guides.
  • Clear prices: what's included and what isn't is listed on every tour.

Get in touch

Tell us when you're travelling and what you'd like to see, and we'll suggest an itinerary. Use the contact form or the booking form on any tour.

pages.title: FAQs
pages.content:
Short answers to the questions travellers ask us most. Can't find yours? Send us a message.

Booking & payment

How far ahead should I book?

As early as you can, especially for spring, autumn and holidays. Booking early also gives you more choice of hotels, riads and camps.

How do I book?

Open the tour, choose your date and number of travellers and send a booking request. We reply by email, usually within 24 hours, to confirm availability and the final price. Nothing is paid on this website.

How do I pay?

A small deposit confirms your booking (by PayPal, bank transfer or Wise). You pay the rest in cash to your driver on the first day, in euros, US dollars or Moroccan dirhams.

What is your cancellation policy?

See our Booking & Cancellation Policy page and read it before you confirm.

Can I change the itinerary?

Yes. Every private tour can be adjusted: change the route or the number of days, add or skip places, and choose accommodation to match your budget. Tell us what you would like and we will plan it with you.

Transport

What vehicles do you use?

It depends on the size of your group: a 4×4 such as a Toyota Land Cruiser Prado for small groups, a Ford Tourneo van, or a Mercedes Sprinter minibus for eight people or more. All are air-conditioned and well maintained.

Are airport transfers included?

We can pick you up at the airport when you arrive and drop you off at the end of the tour. Your driver waits for you in the arrivals hall. Flights are not included.

Which airports can I fly into?

Most international flights land in Marrakech or Casablanca. Fes, Tangier, Agadir, Ouarzazate and Errachidia also have airports, and we can meet you at any of them.

Guides

Who are the drivers?

Local driver-guides we choose for their experience, safe driving and love of their country. Along the way they share the history, traditions and stories of the places you pass.

Do they speak English?

Yes, tours run in English by default. If you would like French, Spanish or another language, ask when you book and we will do our best.

Accommodation

Where will I sleep?

In riads and small guesthouses full of character, and in luxury camps in the Merzouga desert. We only use desert camps with private tents and en-suite bathrooms, never shared facilities.

Do desert tents have a private bathroom?

Yes. Every tent has its own bathroom with a shower.

Can I choose my hotels?

Yes. We suggest a few checked options at each price level and you can mix them. If you have a place in mind, tell us and we will try to book it.

Desert & activities

How far is the Sahara from Marrakech?

Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes are about 560 km from Marrakech, so our desert tours from Marrakech stop for a night on the way, usually in the Dadès Valley.

How far is the Sahara from Fes?

About 500 km, a long day's drive with stops.

How far is the desert from Casablanca?

About 660 km. From Casablanca we recommend at least five days so you don't spend the whole trip in the car.

Do I have to ride a camel?

No. If you prefer, we drive you to the camp by 4×4 at no extra cost. Just tell us in advance.

What else can I do in the desert?

Quad biking, buggy driving, sandboarding and horse riding around Merzouga. We can also arrange a photographer, a romantic dinner in the dunes or a proposal setup.

What can I add to my trip?

Before or after your tour: airport transfers, a guided tour of Marrakech or Fes, a hot air balloon flight, and day trips to Essaouira, the Ouzoud waterfalls, the Ourika Valley, Chefchaouen or Volubilis and Meknes.

Your tour

Private or shared, what's the difference?

On a private tour the vehicle, driver and itinerary are just for your group. On a shared tour you travel with a few other guests (ten at most), which costs less, but you still have your own room and your own tent.

Is a week enough for Morocco?

Yes. Seven days is enough for Marrakech, the Atlas, Aït Benhaddou, the Sahara, Fes and Chefchaouen at a comfortable pace.

Which 7-day route should I take?

It depends on where you land and leave. From Tangier, go via Chefchaouen and Fes to the Sahara and on to Marrakech; from Casablanca, there is a similar loop. Tell us your flights and we will suggest the best route.

Are meals included?

On desert tours, breakfast and dinner are included each night you stay with us; lunches are not, so you can choose where to stop. Each tour page lists exactly what is included.

Can you cater for special diets?

Yes. Tell us about vegetarian, vegan or other needs when you book and we will arrange your meals.

What should I bring to the desert?

Comfortable shoes, a scarf or hat, sunglasses, sunscreen and a warm layer: desert nights are cold, especially from November to March.

pages.title: Booking & Cancellation Policy
pages.content:
Draft: review and adapt this policy before publishing.

Booking

Booking requests sent through this website are not confirmed until we reply by email. Our confirmation states the tour, dates, number of travellers, what is included and the final price.

Payment

Payment terms (deposit, balance and accepted payment methods) are stated in your confirmation email.

Cancellation by you

  • Tours marked Free cancellation can be cancelled free of charge up to 24 hours before the start time.
  • For other tours, the cancellation terms are stated in your confirmation email.
  • To cancel, use My bookings on this website or reply to your confirmation email.

Changes and cancellation by us

If weather, road conditions or events beyond our control make a tour unsafe, we may change the itinerary or cancel. If we cancel, we offer another date or a full refund of any amount paid.

pages.title: Privacy Policy
pages.content:
Draft: review and adapt this policy before publishing.

What we collect

When you send a booking request or a contact message, we collect your name, email, phone number (if you give it), travel dates, number of travellers and your message. If you sign in with Google, we receive your name, email address and profile photo from Google.

How we use it

We use this information only to answer your request, organise your tour and contact you about it. We do not sell your data.

Who we share it with

We share the details needed for your trip with the drivers, guides and camps that run it.

How long we keep it

We keep booking records for as long as needed for accounting and legal reasons, then delete them.

Your rights

You can ask us to see, correct or delete your personal data at any time using the contact form.

pages.title: Terms & Conditions
pages.content:
Draft: review and adapt these terms before publishing.

Our services

We organise tours, day trips, desert camping and activities in Morocco. The details of each tour are described on its page and in your confirmation email.

Your responsibilities

Travellers must have a valid passport and any visa required, and are advised to have travel insurance. Please tell us about any health or mobility needs before booking.

Prices

Prices shown are "from" prices per person, adult or group, as stated. The final price is confirmed by email.

Liability

We take care to run safe tours with experienced staff. We are not responsible for delays or changes caused by weather, road closures or events beyond our control.

Reviews

Reviews you post must be honest and about your own experience. We check reviews before publishing them.
